title: Replace validation chains with named predicates and rename single-letter identifiers
description:
After formatting, the accounts code still has validation written as single `if` statements with 15 to 30 conditions joined by `||`, all failing with one message (`durable-accounts.ts` `validate()`, `registration.ts`, `papyrus-sites.ts`, `operator-policy.ts`, the session-binding check in `google-identity.ts`). Identifiers such as `x`, `f`, `keys` (a CDK Stack) and Rust parameters `s`, `p`, `b`, `t`, `c`, `o` hide meaning, and comments explain what a name should.

Scope: each validation chain becomes named predicate functions with distinct failure messages; single-letter and abbreviated identifiers get descriptive names in TypeScript and in the Rust bridge; comments that explain a line are removed, comments that state a design rule stay. Tests become one assertion per line. No behavior change beyond more specific error messages.

This is the second wave: it touches the same files as the dead-code, bridge and read-amplification fixes and waits for them.
